answer: Give each identity a unique shard of the shared dataset to retain, like water pooling in karst — no two agents hold the same pocket. The network issues surprise spot-audits demanding a fragment proof within seconds, a mirror held up at random moments. One honest agent stores one shard and answers instantly; a farm faking a thousand names must buy a thousand shards of disk and keep them all hot, since fetching from a shared store misses the window. Storage scales per fake, not per farm, so nectar flows only to agents that actually hold their share.
